title: Momentous Nightly Sleep Pack vs a build-your-own magnesium + L-theanine + apigenin stack

bundle.name: Momentous Nightly Sleep, 30 single-serve packs (3 capsules each)

items.name: Magnesium (as magnesium bisglycinate) 200 mg per pack

components.product: Spring Valley High Absorption Magnesium Glycinate Capsules, 200 mg per 2-capsule serving, 120 count

summary: Momentous's sleep pack is just 200 mg magnesium bisglycinate, 200 mg L-theanine and 50 mg apigenin, and you can buy those same three doses separately for about $12 a month instead of $80.
evidence: Momentous's product page lists the supplement facts per pack (3 capsules): magnesium (as magnesium bisglycinate) 200 mg, L-theanine 200 mg and apigenin 50 mg, 30 packs for $79.99 one-time or $59.99 on subscription. Walmart's Spring Valley listing states 200 mg magnesium glycinate per 2-capsule serving (120 capsules = 60 servings). Nutricost's Walmart listings state 200 mg L-theanine per capsule (120 servings) and 50 mg apigenin per capsule (1-capsule serving, 180 count). Retailer listings did not show the full supplement-facts text for the Nutricost products, so confidence is medium; a DSLD-registered alternative for apigenin is Double Wood Apigenin 50 mg (DSLD 286145).
differences: You take 4 capsules from three bottles (2 magnesium, 1 theanine, 1 apigenin) instead of 3 capsules from one packet. Momentous says its apigenin comes from grapefruit; the Nutricost listing doesn't name a source. Momentous also sells the same formula as a 90-capsule, 30-serving jar for $59.99 one-time ($44.99 on subscription), which showed 'estimated to be back in stock soon' when checked; the build-your-own stack still saves about 80% against that jar or the $59.99 pack subscription.

title: Thorne Sleep Stack vs a build-your-own GABA + melatonin + magnesium stack

bundle.name: Thorne Sleep Stack (PharmaGABA-250, Melaton-3, Magnesium Bisglycinate powder)

components.product: Spring Valley Fast-Dissolve Melatonin Tablets, Strawberry, 3 mg, 120 count
Spring Valley High Absorption Magnesium Glycinate Capsules, 200 mg per 2-capsule serving, 120 count

summary: Thorne's $115 Sleep Stack is 250 mg GABA, 3 mg melatonin and 200 mg magnesium bisglycinate, and the same three doses cost about $23 for the same 60 nights from store and value brands.
evidence: NIH DSLD labels confirm Thorne PharmaGABA-250 at 250 mg GABA per capsule, 60 capsules (DSLD 336348), and Melaton-3 at 3 mg melatonin per capsule, 60 capsules (DSLD 298036). Thorne's Magnesium Bisglycinate page and DSLD 284233 show 200 mg magnesium as magnesium bisglycinate per 3.11 g scoop, 60 servings. The Walmart listings show Swanson GABA at 250 mg per capsule (60 count), Spring Valley Fast-Dissolve melatonin at 3 mg per tablet (120 count) and Spring Valley magnesium glycinate at 200 mg per 2 capsules (120 count, 60 servings). Swanson's full supplement-facts panel was not shown on the listing, so confidence is medium.
differences: Thorne uses PharmaGABA, GABA made by fermentation; Swanson's GABA is the same molecule at the same 250 mg dose, but it is not the PharmaGABA ingredient. Thorne's magnesium is a flavored powder (citric acid, monk fruit) you mix in water; the Spring Valley version is 2 capsules. Spring Valley melatonin is a strawberry fast-dissolve tablet rather than a swallowed capsule. You get 60 extra melatonin tablets in the bottle. The 60-day supply assumes 1 GABA capsule a night; Thorne's label allows up to 3 a day.

summary: Thorne's two-product athlete sleep stack is 3 mg melatonin plus 200 mg magnesium bisglycinate, and Spring Valley sells both doses for about $14 for the same 60 nights.
evidence: Thorne's stack page lists Melaton-3 (60) and Magnesium Bisglycinate (60 scoops) for $62. NIH DSLD 298036 shows Melaton-3 at 3 mg melatonin per capsule, 60 capsules, and Thorne's Magnesium Bisglycinate page (and DSLD 284233) shows 200 mg magnesium as magnesium bisglycinate per scoop, 60 servings. Walmart lists Spring Valley Fast-Dissolve Melatonin at 3 mg per tablet (120 count, $5.36) and Spring Valley magnesium glycinate at 200 mg per 2-capsule serving (120 capsules, $10.87). The Spring Valley listings did not show full supplement-facts panels, so confidence is medium.
differences: Thorne's magnesium is a powder (with citric acid and monk fruit) that you stir into water; Spring Valley's is 2 capsules. Thorne's melatonin is a swallowed capsule; Spring Valley's is a strawberry fast-dissolve tablet.

title: Momentous Anti-Inflammatory Stack vs Doctor's Best Meriva + Nutricost creatine + Spring Valley D3

bundle.name: Momentous Anti-Inflammatory Stack for Women (Turmeric, Creatine, Vitamin D3), 30 servings

items.name: Momentous Vitamin D3 2000 IU, 60 liquid capsules

components.product: Doctor's Best Curcumin Phytosome with Meriva, 180 veggie capsules (1,000 mg per 2 capsules)
Nutricost Creatine Monohydrate Micronized Powder, Unflavored, 500 g, 100 servings
Spring Valley Vitamin D3 Softgels, 50 mcg (2,000 IU), 400 count

summary: Momentous's anti-inflammatory stack is 1,000 mg Meriva turmeric, 5 g creatine and 2,000 IU D3, and the same doses from Doctor's Best, Nutricost and Spring Valley cost about $27 a month instead of $80.
evidence: Momentous's stack page lists the supplement facts: Turmeric with Meriva 1,000 mg per 2 capsules (turmeric standardized to 18% curcuminoids, 30 servings), Creatine 5 g creatine monohydrate per scoop (30 servings) and Vitamin D3 50 mcg (2,000 IU) per capsule (60 servings), $79.97 one-time. NIH DSLD 302652 confirms Doctor's Best Curcumin Phytosome with Meriva at 1,000 mg Meriva per 2 capsules, min. 18% (180 mg) curcuminoids, 90 servings. The creatine and D3 alternatives are the already-verified Nutricost creatine (5 g per serving, 100 servings) and Spring Valley D3 (50 mcg per softgel) pairs.
differences: Momentous's D3 is plant-based (vegan) cholecalciferol in olive oil; Spring Valley D3 is a standard softgel and is not labeled vegan. Momentous describes its own 'Signature Spec' creatine; Nutricost is micronized creatine monohydrate. The Momentous stack page showed 'estimated to be back in stock soon' when checked. The upfront cost of the full alternative packs ($87.87) is higher than one stack, but it covers 3 months of turmeric, more than 3 months of creatine and over a year of D3.
